<description>
`CSHA512::Finalize()` leaves the digest in the hasher's state and the last block in its buffer, and the class never wipes them. Every `CSHA512` outside tests and benchmarks hashes secret data: in `CCrypter::BytesToKeySHA512AES` the final state holds the key and IV derived from the passphrase, the two hashers in `CHMAC_SHA512` hold BIP32 seed and key material, and the RNG hashers in `random.cpp` hold seed material.

I add a destructor that cleanses both, as `ChaCha20` already does, so each hasher is wiped when it goes out of scope instead of by each caller. Following review, this replaces the one-line cleanse in `crypter.cpp` this PR first proposed. It also makes #36551 unnecessary. A test is impractical, since the object no longer exists once destroyed. I built the tree and ran `test_bitcoin` and `ctest`; both pass, and Core's warning flags report nothing new.
</description>
